text: These are David son of Jesse's final recorded words — words from the man lifted up high, the one anointed by Jacob's God, Israel's favorite singer of songs.
The LORD's Spirit spoke through me, David said; his message was on my tongue.
Israel's God spoke, the Rock of Israel told me: whoever governs people fairly, ruling in reverence toward God,
is like the morning sun breaking over a cloudless sky, like the shine after rain that makes grass push up out of the ground.

Isn't my own family right with him this way? Hasn't he made a lasting covenant with me, spelled out and guaranteed in every part — won't he bring about all my rescue and give me everything I long for?
But wicked men are like thorns, every one of them, thrown aside — nobody picks those up with bare hands.
Whoever deals with thorns needs iron tools or a spear shaft, and they're simply burned up on the spot.
Here are the names of David's elite fighters: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahkemonite led the Three; he once raised his spear against eight hundred men and struck them all down in a single encounter.
After him came Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three great warriors who stood with David when they mocked the Philistines gathered for battle there — the Israelite troops had pulled back,

but Eleazar held his ground and kept cutting down Philistines until his arm gave out and his hand locked onto the sword; the LORD gave a huge victory that day, and the soldiers only came back afterward to strip the bodies.
Next was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines had massed at a spot with a field full of lentils, and Israel's men ran from them,
but Shammah planted himself in the middle of that field, held it, and cut the Philistines down — another great victory the LORD brought about.
At harvest time, three of the thirty leading warriors traveled down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a Philistine unit was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was staying in the stronghold then, with a Philistine garrison stationed at Bethlehem.
David felt a deep craving and said, if only someone would bring me water from the well by Bethlehem's gate!

So the three warriors forced their way through the Philistine camp, drew water from that well by Bethlehem's gate, and carried it back to David — but he wouldn't drink it; instead he poured it out before the LORD.
He said, LORD, I could never do this — would I drink the blood of men who risked their own lives? And so he refused to drink it. That's the kind of thing these three warriors did.
Abishai, Joab's brother and the son of Zeruiah, was chief over the Thirty; he once fought off three hundred men with his spear and killed them, earning fame alongside the Three.
He was honored above the rest of the Thirty and became their commander, yet he never quite reached the standing of the Three.

Benaiah son of Jehoiada, a brave fighter from Kabzeel, accomplished great feats — he struck down two of Moab's best warriors, and on a day when snow had fallen he climbed down into a pit and killed a lion there.
He also killed a massive Egyptian. The Egyptian carried a spear, but Benaiah went at him armed only with a club, tore the spear out of the man's grip, and killed him with his own weapon.
These were the kinds of things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and they earned him a reputation alongside the three great warriors.
He was more honored than anyone in the Thirty, though he didn't reach the level of the Three; David put him in charge of his personal guard.
Among the Thirty were Asahel, Joab's brother; Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem;
Shammah the Harodite; Elika the Harodite;
Helez the Paltite; Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa;
Abiezer from Anathoth; Mebunnai the Hushathite;
Zalmon the Ahohite; Maharai the Netophathite;
Heleb son of Baanah the Netophathite; Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah, in Benjamin's territory;
Benaiah the Pirathonite; Hiddai from the ravines near Gaash;
Abi-albon the Arbathite; Azmaveth the Barhumite;
Eliahba the Shaalbonite; the sons of Jashen; Jonathan;
Shammah the Hararite; Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite;
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite; Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;
Hezro the Carmelite; Paarai the Arbite;
Igal son of Nathan from Zobah; Bani the Gadite;
Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai the Beerothite, who carried Joab son of Zeruiah's armor;
Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
and Uriah the Hittite — thirty-seven men in all.
